The next step is to keep using Claude Code normally, ideally in your other projects, and let detection run. The M3 check needs a day of that. You don't have to do anything in this repo for it.

While it runs, keep an eye on two things:
- **Near-duplicates:** the same idea stored twice under different names.
- **Snippets on code-heavy turns:** whether they quote real code or still quote chat text.

`jq` on `~/.local/share/tutor-agent/concepts.json` shows both.

Meanwhile, I recommend starting M4 (the tutor pane) now rather than waiting. It doesn't depend on the outcome of the M3 check: if detection needs tuning, that's a prompt change in the detector, and M4 only reads the concept store. Having the pane soon also makes the review easier than reading JSON.

Then, at the end of the day:
1. Add the findings to the M6 log.
2. Tick the M3 checkbox, or open a fix if snippets or duplicates are a problem.
3. Update the status line in `CLAUDE.md`.

the old or the new version, never a half-written one. Writers take an exclusive `flock` on a
separate lock file, so two processes can't both read version N and overwrite each other's change.

one concept behind what it did. They have a CS degree but little practical experience, and want
senior-level understanding. Skip basics. Be short and concrete: start from the code, not theory.

Write the lesson in Markdown with exactly these sections:

## What the agent did
Quote the relevant part of the snippet in a fenced code block (trim it to the lines that matter),
then say in one or two sentences what it does.

## Why it did it

## The general concept

def seed(*names: str) -> ConceptStore:
    store = ConceptStore()
    store.record([Entry(n, "Design patterns", f"About {n}.",
                        Source(snippet=f"code for {n}", context="ctx", project="/home/me/Projects/api"))

def run(test, store=None, size=(120, 40)):
    """Run `test(pilot, app)` inside a headless app."""
    async def main():
        app = TutorApp(store=store or ConceptStore(), cfg=Settings(), poll_s=0.05)
        async with app.run_test(size=size) as pilot:

def test_lesson_has_the_structure_and_quotes_the_snippet():
    event = batches.load("supervisor-loop")[3]  # the edit of supervisor.py

        id="supervisor-with-last-known-good-rollback", name="Supervisor with last-known-good rollback",

                        project="~/Projects/project-d", file=event.file)],
    )
    text = lessons.generate(concept, Settings()).text

    positions = [text.find(s) for s in SECTIONS]
    assert all(p >= 0 for p in positions), f"missing sections in:\n{text}"
    assert positions == sorted(positions), "sections out of order"

    code_lines = {line.strip() for line in snippet.splitlines() if len(line.strip()) > 15}
    assert any(line in quoted for line in code_lines), "no line of the real snippet is quoted"

    links = re.findall(r"https?://\S+", text[positions[4]:])
    assert 2 <= len(links) <= 3, links
    assert len(text.split()) < 700

# 0028: Lesson format, lesson cache files, and tutor pane behaviour

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-13

## Context
M4 builds the tutor pane and lessons. [0017](0017-lesson-cache.md) says lessons are cached per concept, but not in what form. [0009](0009-textual-tui.md) picks Textual, but not how the pane notices new concepts or when it spends an LLM call. Follow-ups in M5 need the lesson and the source it was built from ([0012](0012-stateless-follow-ups.md)).

## Decision
- **Lesson call:** one plain-text `claude -p` call on `lesson_model` (no `--json-schema`). The prompt holds the concept's name, category, summary, and the **most recent source** (project, file, context, snippet). The snippet sits in a backtick fence longer than any run inside it. The system prompt fixes five Markdown sections in the [teaching-strategy](../pedagogy/teaching-strategy.md) order, at most 500 words, and 2–3 links it is confident exist.
- **Lesson cache:** `lessons/<concept_id>.json` in the data directory, one file per concept, with `text`, `model`, `generated_at`, and a copy of the **source** the lesson was built from. Written to a temp file and swapped in with `os.replace`. A file that can't be parsed counts as missing and is replaced on the next open. Only the pane writes it, so there is no lock.
- **When the pane calls the model:** highlighting a concept shows its cached lesson, or a card (summary, context, "press Enter") if there is none. It never makes a call. **Enter** opens the lesson: `new` becomes `seen`, and the lesson is generated if it isn't cached. **r** regenerates it.
- **Responsiveness:** the call runs in a Textual worker thread. The lesson area shows a loading state, and the list and keys keep working. A failed call is logged and shown under the card, and nothing is cached.
- **New concepts:** the pane checks the concept file's mtime and size once a second and reloads when they change. Readers never take the store lock, so the detector is never slowed down.
